title: Marathi Negative Sentences: नाही, नको & Don't
description: How to say no, not and don't in Marathi — the आहे→नाही flip and नको for “don't want”, with curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
secondaryKeywords: how to say no in marathi
intro: Marathi negation has three everyday tools: नाही (is not / no — the opposite of आहे), नको (don't want), and नका (don't — the negative command). The grammar notes below come straight from Unit 02 of the Bol Marathi curriculum, where असणे (to be) is taught first positive, then negative.

Hindi speakers: the skeleton is familiar — आहे flips to नाही the way है flips to नहीं. The Marathi-specific parts are नको (want-negation is its own word, not नाही पाहिजे) and word-final placement in commands.
tip: Learn the pair together: पाहिजे (need/want) ↔ नको (don't want). They are used hundreds of times a day.

sections.heading: नाही — the आहे flip
paragraphs: Positive: मी तयार आहे (I am ready). Negative: मी तयार नाही. The verb-be negates in place; nothing else in the sentence moves. Unit 06 even drills the question form: कळतंय का? — नाही, कळत नाही (Understood? — No, didn’t understand).
This is the single highest-frequency transformation in spoken Marathi. Get आहे ↔ नाही automatic and half of survival Marathi opens up.

sections.heading: नको — don't want is one word
paragraphs: Hindi splits it: नहीं चाहिए. Marathi fuses it: नको. The real Unit 02 sentence मला चहा नको, पाणी द्या (no tea, give water) shows the pair in action: पाहिजे for “need”, नको for “don't want”. Saying मला चहा नाही पाहिजे is understandable but not what people say.
For telling someone not to do something, the negative imperative is नका: that form appears in Unit 02’s imperative lessons alongside polite requests.

mistakes.wrong: मला चहा नाही पाहिजे for “I don't want tea”
mistakes.right: मला चहा नको
mistakes.why: नको is its own word — it is not assembled from नाही + पाहिजे.

mistakes.wrong: Moving नाही to the front like English “not”
mistakes.right: Keep नाही where आहे stood: मी तयार नाही
mistakes.why: Marathi negates the verb in place; the sentence order stays verb-final.

mcq.question: “I am not ready” in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: आहे flips to नाही in place.

mcq.question: Which word means “don't want”?
mcq.explanation: नको = don't want; नका = don't (command); नाही = is not.

translate.source: मुझे चाय नहीं चाहिए, पानी दीजिए।
translate.note: The real Unit 02 sentence — नको carries the whole negation.

faq.question: How do you say “no” in Marathi?
faq.answer: नाही (nāhī). To negate a sentence, flip आहे to नाही: मी तयार आहे → मी तयार नाही.

faq.question: What is the difference between नको and नाही?
faq.answer: नाही negates “is” (आहे → नाही). नको means “don't want” (पाहिजे → नको). And नका means “don't” in commands.

title: Marathi Commands & Polite Requests: या, जा, द्या
description: Marathi imperatives and polite requests — या, द्या, बसा, कृपया — with curriculum examples, Hindi comparison and cultural etiquette notes.
intro: Marathi commands are short and verb-first-feeling: या (come), जा (go), खा (eat), द्या (give). Add कृपया (please) or use the polite request forms and blunt commands become courteous ones. The notes below are the verified Unit 02 imperative and polite-request lessons, plus Unit 13's cultural-etiquette note.

Hindi speakers: the roots look familiar (आइए/जाइए/खाइए → या/जा/खा), but Marathi polite forms are terser. The tune of politeness comes from कृपया placement and the honorific तुम्ही rather than long verb endings.
tip: Default to कृपया with strangers and elders; bare imperatives are for friends, children and urgency.

sections.heading: From blunt to polite
paragraphs: या! (come!) works in an emergency; कृपया इथे या (please come here) works with a stranger — the real Unit 02 sentence. बसा (sit) becomes respectful as राव, कसे आहात? कृपया बस्या from Unit 05's honorific lesson.
Festival and home etiquette (Unit 13) layers on top: greetings, taking blessings, and the softeners that keep commands sounding like invitations.

mistakes.right: Add कृपया or the honorific tone: कृपया बसा
mistakes.why: Marathi marks respect through कृपया, तुम्ही and honorific address rather than Hindi-style -इए endings alone.

mistakes.right: Use नका: इथे जाऊ नका (don't go here)
mistakes.why: नाही negates statements; नका negates commands.

mcq.question: Which word turns a blunt command into a polite request?

fill.hint: The Unit 02 sentence — imperative of येणे.

translate.note: From Unit 09 — command + कृपया, polite anywhere.

faq.question: How do you say “please” in Marathi?
faq.answer: कृपया (kr̥payā) — same word as Hindi. Place it before or after the command: कृपया इथे या / बिल द्या, कृपया.

faq.question: How do Marathi imperatives differ from Hindi?
faq.answer: Roots overlap (या/जा/खा), but Marathi polite requests are shorter; respect is carried by कृपया and the तुम्ही form instead of long -इए endings.

title: Marathi Possessives: माझा, माझी, माझं Explained
description: My, your, his in Marathi: माझा/माझी/माझं agree with the owned noun's gender — with curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
intro: Marathi has three genders — masculine, feminine and neuter — and possessives agree with the thing owned, not the owner: माझा भाऊ (my brother), माझी बहीण (my sister), माझं पुस्तक (my book). The notes below come from Unit 02's possession lesson and Unit 03's adjective-agreement lesson.
Hindi speakers already know agreement (मेरा/मेरी); the new work is the third gender. नाव, पुस्तक, कुटुंब, पाणी are all neuter and take माझं.
tip: Learn every new noun together with its possessive: माझं पुस्तक, माझी बहीण — gender comes free that way.

sections.heading: The three-way split
paragraphs: माझा for masculine nouns, माझी for feminine, माझं for neuter. The curriculum sentences make it concrete: हे माझं पुस्तक आहे (this is my book — neuter), ही माझी बहीण आहे (this is my sister — feminine), माझं कुटुंब मोठं आहे (my family is big — neuter again).
Unit 03's adjective-agreement note extends the same logic to describing words — once possessives agree, adjectives follow the same three genders.

mistakes.right: माझं नाव — नाव is neuter
mistakes.why: Hindi मेरा नाम misleads: Marathi नाव takes the neuter possessive.

mistakes.wrong: Agreement with the owner instead of the noun
mistakes.right: A woman says माझा भाऊ too — the brother is masculine
mistakes.why: The possessive matches the owned thing's gender, not the speaker's — same logic as Hindi, one more gender.

fill.sentence: हे ___ पुस्तक आहे. (This is MY book.)

faq.question: How many genders does Marathi have?
faq.answer: Three: masculine, feminine and neuter — and possessives (माझा/माझी/माझं) agree with the gender of the thing owned.

faq.question: Is माझं for plural?
faq.answer: No — माझं is neuter singular. Plural possessives (माझे/माझ्या/माझीं) are covered inside Units 02–03 along with the agreement rules.

title: Marathi Ability & Obligation: Can, Must, Should
description: How to say can, must, should and need-to in Marathi — शकतो, पाहिजे, गरज आहे — with Unit 04 curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
intro: Three modal patterns from Unit 04 (Lessons 5-6) mapped English to Marathi: ability (शकतो), obligation (पाहिजे/गरज आहे), and recommendation (करावं). Each maps the English modal to the Marathi construction with the grammar note.

English can/must/should each split into distinct Marathi forms: शकतो (can/able to), पाहिजे (must/need to), गरज आहे (necessary), करावं (should). The grammar is verb-root based, not auxiliary-based like English.
tip: शकतो = can (ability), पाहिजे = must (need), करावं = should. Learn the verb-root pattern: करणे → करावं, येणे → यावं, जाणे → जावं.

sections.heading: Can / able to — शकतो
paragraphs: English "I can swim" → Marathi मी पवणे शकतो. The pattern: subject + verb-infinitive + शकतो (masc) / शकते (fem) / शकते (neut). The verb stays in infinitive; शकणे takes the agreement.

sections.heading: Must / have to — पाहिजे / गरज आहे
paragraphs: English "I must go" → मी जावं पाहिजे (or मी जावं गरज आहे). The pattern: verb-root + व + पाहिजे (जावं, खावं, बोलावं). गरज आहे is slightly more formal; both mean obligation.

sections.heading: Should / ought to — करावं
paragraphs: English "You should study" → तुम्ही अभ्यास करावं. The pattern: verb-root + व + करावं (करावं, जावं, खावं). This is the recommendation/advice form — softer than पाहिजे.

mistakes.right: शकतो / शकत नाही
mistakes.why: English can/can't are auxiliaries; Marathi uses the verb शकणे with infinitive.

mistakes.wrong: Saying मी जाऊ पाहिजे for must
mistakes.right: मी जावं पाहिजे — root + व
mistakes.why: The obligation form adds व to the root before पाहिजे: जा → जावं, खा → खावं, कर → करावं.

mistakes.right: पाहिजे / गरज आहे — चहिए has no Marathi life
mistakes.why: Hindi चाहिए maps to पाहिजे or गरज आहे; there is no direct cognate.

mcq.question: "I can speak Marathi" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: मी मराठी बोलू शकतो — infinitive + शकतो.

mcq.question: "You must study" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तुम्ही अभ्यास पाहिजे — obligation takes पाहिजे.

mcq.question: "He should eat" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: तो खावं करावं — should takes root+व+करावं.

translate.answer: तुम्ही मला मदत करणे शकता का?

translate.note: Obligation — root य् + व + पाहिजे = यावं.

faq.question: How do you say "can" in Marathi?
faq.answer: Use verb + शकतो (masc) / शकते (fem/neut): करणे → करू शकतो, येणे → येऊ शकते.

faq.question: What is the difference between पाहिजे and करावं?
faq.answer: पाहिजे = must/need (obligation). करावं = should/ought to (recommendation). पाहिजे is stronger.

title: Marathi Compound Verbs: Root + Auxiliary Patterns
description: Marathi compound verbs — give up, start doing, finish doing, try to — root + auxiliary patterns (देऊन द्या, सुरू करा, संपवा, प्रयत्न करा) from Unit 04.
intro: Marathi builds complex meanings by pairing a main verb with an auxiliary: देऊन द्या (give up/hand over), सुरू करा (start), संपवा (finish), प्रयत्न करा (try). Unit 04 (Lessons 3-4) teaches these as ready-to-use patterns — the main verb takes the -ऊन/-ून form, then the auxiliary carries the tense.
Hindi speakers recognize the logic (दे देना, शुरू करना, समाप्त करना) — the Marathi forms are देऊन द्या, सुरू करा, संपवा, प्रयत्न करा. The auxiliaries are द्या, करा, संपवा, प्रयत्न करा.
tip: Verb + -ऊन/-ून + auxiliary: खाऊन द्या (eat up), सुरू करा (start), संपवा (finish), प्रयत्न करा (try). The -ऊन form is the Marathi conjunctive participle.

sections.heading: The four everyday compounds
paragraphs: 1) देऊन द्या — give up / hand over / let go: मला कागद देऊन द्या (hand me the paper). 2) सुरू करा — start: सुरू करा वाचणे (start reading). 3) संपवा — finish: संपवा वाचणे (finish reading). 4) प्रयत्न करा — try: प्रयत्न करा वाचण्याचा (try reading).

sections.heading: The -ऊन form — the connector
paragraphs: The main verb takes -ऊन (करून, खाऊन, बोलून, वाचून) and the auxiliary carries the tense: खाऊन दिला (gave to eat / fed), सुरू केले (started), संपवले (finished), प्रयत्न केले (tried). The auxiliary (द्या, करा, संपवा, प्रयत्न करा) conjugates normally.

mistakes.right: Main verb must take -ऊन: खाऊन द्या (not खा द्या)
mistakes.why: The -ऊन form is the conjunctive participle — it connects the action to the auxiliary. Omitting it breaks the grammar.

mistakes.right: खाऊन द्या — feed = eat + give
mistakes.why: The logic is action + transfer. खाऊन द्या = eat + give = feed someone. खा द्या is ungrammatical.

mcq.question: "Start reading" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: वाचून सुरू करा — verb + ऊन + सुरू करा.

mcq.question: "Try to speak" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: बोलून प्रयत्न करा — verb + ऊन + प्रयत्न करा.

faq.question: What is the -ऊन form in Marathi?
faq.answer: The conjunctive participle — connects main verb to auxiliary: करून, खाऊन, बोलून, वाचून. It means "having done X" and attaches to auxiliaries like द्या, करा, संपवा.

faq.question: How do you say "start doing" in Marathi?
faq.answer: सुरू करा + verb-ऊन: वाचून सुरू करा (start reading), खाऊन सुरू करा (start eating).

title: Marathi Counting & Quantifiers: Numbers, Fractions
description: Marathi counting, quantifiers and fractions — एक, दोन, तीन, पाव, आधा, दोन किलो — with Unit 03 curriculum examples and Hindi comparison.
intro: Marathi counting and quantifiers from Unit 03 (Lessons 4-5): cardinal numbers, fractions (पाव, आधा, दोन तिसरा), classifiers for people/things, and the agreement rules with nouns. The notes come from Unit 03's counting and quantifier lessons.

Hindi speakers: the numbers are nearly identical (एक, दोन, तीन, चार, पाच...). The new work is the fractions (पाव = 1/4, आधा = 1/2, सवा = 1.25, डेढ = 1.5) and the classifier agreement (दोन माणस = two people, दोन पुस्तके = two books).
tip: पाव = 1/4, आधा = 1/2, सवा = 1¼, डेढ = 1½ — these combine with numbers: सवा दोन = 2.25, डेढ तीन = 3.5. The pattern is the same as Hindi.

sections.heading: Fractions — the daily-use ones
paragraphs: पाव (1/4), आधा (1/2), सवा (1¼), डेढ (1½). They combine with whole numbers: सवा दोन (2.25), डेढ तीन (3.5), पाव चार (3.75). The pattern matches Hindi exactly — पाव, आधा, सवा, डेढ.

sections.heading: Classifiers — people vs things
paragraphs: दोन माणस (two people — human classifier), दोन पुस्तके (two books — neuter plural), तीन कुटुंब (three families — neuter). The classifier agreement follows the noun gender, not the number itself.

mistakes.right: एक (masc), एक (fem — same form), एक (neut — same form) — form is same, agreement shows on adjective/noun
mistakes.why: एक is invariant; the gender shows on what follows: एक मोठा घर, एक मोठी बहीण, एक मोठं पुस्तक.

mistakes.wrong: Saying दोन आदमी for two men
mistakes.right: दोन माणस — माणस is the human classifier
mistakes.why: आदमी is Hindi; माणस is the Marathi human classifier used with numbers.

mistakes.right: सवा दोन — correct; but सवा दोन is 2.25, सवा तीन is 3.25
mistakes.why: सवा + number = number + 1/4. सवा दोन = 2 + 0.25 = 2.25. The pattern is consistent.

mcq.question: Two and a half in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: डेढ = 1.5, but for 2.5 the pattern is सवा दोन? Wait — 2.5 = ढाई (Hindi) / अढाई (Marathi). The course teaches सवा/डेढ/पाव/आधा for fractions with whole numbers.

mcq.question: Two people in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: दोन माणस — माणस is the human classifier.

faq.question: What are the main Marathi fractions?
faq.answer: पाव (1/4), आधा (1/2), सवा (1.25), डेढ (1.5) — they combine with whole numbers: सवा दोन (2.25), डेढ तीन (3.5).

faq.question: How do you say "two people" in Marathi?
faq.answer: दोन माणस — माणस is the human classifier used with numbers instead of आदमी.

title: Marathi Passive & Causative: केला जाते, खववते
description: Marathi passive and causative constructions — passive (केला जाते, खाल्ले जाते), causative (खववते, बोलवते) — from Unit 21 advanced grammar.
intro: Passive and causative from Unit 21 (Lessons 5-6): passive voice (केला जाते — is done, खाल्ले जाते — is eaten) and causative (खववते — makes eat, बोलवते — makes speak). Each construction maps the Hindi pattern to the Marathi morphology with the grammar shift.

Passive: past participle + याचे + जाते (केला जाते, खाल्ले जाते, लिहिले जाते). Causative: verb-root + व/वव + ते (खववते = makes eat, बोलवते = makes speak, लिहवते = makes write). The relative-correlative pair is जो…तो (not जो…वह).
tip: Passive = past participle + याचे + जाते. Causative = root + व/वव + ते. Relative = जो…तो. Three patterns, infinite sentences.

sections.heading: Passive — the याचे+जाते frame
paragraphs: Hindi किया जाता है → Marathi केला जाते. The pattern: past participle (केला, खाल्ले, केले, लिहिले) + याचे + जाते. The agent (by whom) uses कडून: मी कडून केला जाते (done by me). The passive verb agrees with the object (केला जाते — masc, केली जाते — fem, केले जाते — neut).

sections.heading: Causative — the व/वव marker
paragraphs: Hindi करवाता है → Marathi करवते. खववते (makes eat = खा + वव + ते), बोलवते (makes speak = बोल + व + ते), लिहवते (makes write = लिही + व + ते), पडवते (makes fall/read). The causative marker व/वव attaches to the verb root before the tense ending. Some verbs are inherently causative (बोलवणे = to make speak); adding another व creates double causative — ungrammatical.

mistakes.wrong: Using किया जाता है structure directly
mistakes.right: केला जाते — past participle + याचे + जाते
mistakes.why: Marathi passive is not a word-for-word translation of Hindi passive; the morphology is different.

mistakes.right: जो…तो — the correlative is तो, not वह
mistakes.why: Marathi's relative-correlative pair is जो…तो. वह never appears as the correlate.

mistakes.right: Check if the verb is already causative (बोलवणे = to make speak); double causative is ungrammatical
mistakes.why: Some verbs are inherently causative; adding another व creates nonsense.

mcq.question: Passive of "to do" in Marathi?
mcq.explanation: केला जाते — past participle केला + याचे + जाते.

mcq.question: Causative of "to eat" (खाणे)?
mcq.explanation: खववते — root खा + वव + ते = makes eat.

faq.question: How do you form the passive in Marathi?
faq.answer: Past participle + याचे + जाते — e.g., केला जाते (is done), खाल्ले जाते (is eaten), लिहिले जाते (is written).

faq.question: What is the causative of "to speak" (बोलणे)?
faq.answer: बोलवते — root बोल + व + ते = makes speak.

title: Marathi Frequency Adverbs: Always, Never, Sometimes, Daily
description: Marathi frequency adverbs — नेहमी (always), कधीच (never), कधीकधी (sometimes), रोज (daily) — with Unit 18 curriculum examples and sentence position rules.
intro: Frequency adverbs from Unit 18 (Lesson 5) and the Adverbs vocabulary category (30 words): नेहमी (always), कधीच (never), कधीकधी (sometimes), रोज (daily), लगेच (immediately), हळूहळू (slowly), पुन्हा (again), अजून (still/yet). Each shows the Marathi, English, Hindi, and the sentence-position rule.

The position rule is absolute: frequency adverbs sit immediately before the verb. मी रोज क्रिकेट खेळतो (I play cricket daily) — never मी क्रिकेट खेळतो रोज. The Adverbs vocabulary category (30 words) includes मुद्दाम (deliberately), चुकून (by mistake), एकत्र (together), एकटा (alone) and directional adverbs (बाहेरून, आतून, वरून, खालून, समोरून).
tip: Position rule: adverb immediately before verb. मी रोज खेळतो — never मी खेळतो रोज. कधीच (never) = कधी (when) + च (negating particle).

sections.heading: The frequency ladder
paragraphs: नेहमी (always) → रोज (daily) → कधीकधी (sometimes) → कधीच (never). The च particle negates: कधी (when) → कधीच (never). नेहमी and कधीच are opposites; रोज and कधीकधी fill the middle.

sections.heading: Position rule — absolute
paragraphs: Adverb immediately before the verb: मी रोज क्रिकेट खेळतो, मी कधीकधी चित्रकला करतो. Never at the end. This rule holds for all 30 adverbs in the category — directionals too: बाहेरून आला (came from outside).

mistakes.right: Adverb before verb: मी रोज खेळतो (not मी खेळतो रोज)
mistakes.why: Unit 18 pattern — adverbs pre-verb, consistently. This is the single most common word-order error.

mistakes.right: कधी = when; कधीच = never
mistakes.why: The च particle negates — a tiny suffix, a total meaning flip.

mistakes.right: अजून = still; अजूनही = yet/still (emphatic)
mistakes.why: The emphatic ही adds the "up to now" nuance.

translate.note: Unit 18 sentence — adverb रोज before verb खेळतो.

faq.question: Where do frequency adverbs go in a Marathi sentence?
faq.answer: Immediately before the verb — मी रोज खेळतो, मी कधीकधी खेळतो. Never at the end.

faq.question: How do you say "never" in Marathi?
faq.answer: कधीच — from कधी (when) + च (negating particle). The opposite of नेहमी (always).

title: Marathi Demonstratives: This, That, Here, There
description: Marathi demonstratives — this/that (हा/ही/हे, तो/ती/ते), here/there (इथे/तिथे) — with Unit 05 examples and gender agreement rules.
intro: Demonstratives from Unit 05 (Lesson 2): this/that (हा/ही/हे, तो/ती/ते), here/there (इथे/तिथे), like-this/like-that (असा/तसा). Each set agrees in gender — masculine, feminine, neuter — matching the noun they point to.

Hindi speakers: the near/far split (यह/वह, यहाँ/वहाँ) maps directly. The new work is the neuter gender (हे/ते) and the consistent gender agreement across all sets (हा/ही/हे, तो/ती/ते, इथे/तिथे, असा/तसा).
tip: Gender follows the noun: हा पेन (masc), ही बहीण (fem), हे पाणी (neut). The same split applies to तो/ती/ते, इथे/तिथे, असा/तसा.

sections.heading: The three-gender grid
paragraphs: Near (this/here/like-this): हा (masc), ही (fem), हे (neut), इथे (here), असा (like-this). Far (that/there/like-that): तो (masc), ती (fem), ते (neut), तिथे (there), तसा (like-that). The gender is always marked on the demonstrative, never on the noun alone.

sections.heading: Agreement chain — possessives, adjectives, demonstratives
paragraphs: Once you know हा/ही/हे for a noun, the same gender carries to possessives (माझा/माझी/माझं), adjectives (मोठा/मोठी/मोठे), and relatives (जो/जी/जे). The grid is one system, not three separate memorizations.

mistakes.wrong: Using हा for a feminine noun
mistakes.right: ही for feminine: ही बहीण, ही खुर्ची, ही पुस्तक
mistakes.why: The demonstrative must match the noun's gender. हा बहीण is ungrammatical — the sister is feminine, so ही.

mistakes.right: इथे/तिथे are locative — no gender, just near/far
mistakes.why: इथे = here (near speaker), तिथे = there (away). They don't agree with a noun; they point to location.

mistakes.wrong: Using असा for a masculine noun
mistakes.right: असा matches the noun: असा पेन (masc), अशी बहीण (fem), असे पाणी (neut)
mistakes.why: Like-this/like-that carries gender too — the same split as हा/ही/हे.

faq.question: How many genders do Marathi demonstratives have?
faq.answer: Three — masculine (हा/तो), feminine (ही/ती), neuter (हे/ते). The demonstrative always matches the noun's gender.

faq.question: What is the difference between इथे and तिथे?
faq.answer: इथे = here (near the speaker), तिथे = there (away from the speaker). They are locative and do not carry gender.
